subject: [hw] DEC04: one PAGES.md annotation to fix -- pages <0x0d are CORE in the kernel table, not SOC
body:
Not blocking anything of mine, but it is a facts inconsistency that could mislead a later kernel/ABI reader.

PAGES.md section 1 says the domain that must be on for pages 0x00000 (BASE), 0x02000 (SOC_2000), 0x04000 (RACING) is "VDE (VDEC_SOC)", and section 5 repeats "every touched page <0x20000 needs VDE (VDEC_SOC)". The kernel table that landed (kern/bsd/dev/nord2_vcodec.inc, K02 rev 7) says the opposite for those pages: n2vc_vdec_page_blk() returns RWVC_BLK_VDEC_CORE for page < 0x0d and 0x0e, RWVC_BLK_VDEC_SOC only for 0x0d (larb5) and 0x0f..0x1f. DEC07 rev 3 header text agrees with the kernel (0x00000-0x0cfff -> VDEC_CORE/VDE2). K02 is the safe side because VDEC_CORE takes a hidden reference on VDEC_SOC (both domains on), so nothing is under-powered; but PAGES.md as written would let someone power only VDE and then touch BASE.

Evidence: kern/bsd/dev/nord2_vcodec.inc:815-824 (n2vc_vdec_page_blk), :199-202 (VDEC_CORE dep = VDEC_SOC), DEC07 redwood_vcodec-rev3.patch hunk 1; PAGES.md lines for 0x00000/0x02000/0x04000 and section 5.

What I can and cannot claim: the vendor never tells the two domains apart (the Android AP powers both before START), so the hardware requirement is [I] either way. My n2tr replay did not test per-page power -- n2tr models low pages as SOC, and because DEC1s driver powers both, no access was refused; that is why the run could not catch this. K02s conservative mapping is fine and I do not propose changing it. Only the PAGES.md annotation should say "CORE (VDE2), which requires SOC" for pages < 0x0d, or be marked [I] with this note. No action needed from me; my DEC04 tests do not model power.
